headlines.title: Preliminary 2.8 magnitude earthquake strikes near Gilroy
headlines.description: A preliminary 2.8 magnitude earthquake struck near Gilroy, according to the United States Geological Survey. The quake, which hit at 7:04 a.m., was centered 6.5 miles east-southeast, the USGS said. Further information was not immediately available. This is a developing story. Details may change as more information becomes available. Stay tuned for updates. headlines.title: ‘I love what I do': Lifeguard behind Santa Cruz beach rescue releases statement
headlines.description: The teenage lifeguard who saved a young swimmer at Seabright Beach in Santa Cruz on Saturday issued a statement on Wednesday, in which he included details from that day and added he feels “grateful” to have been able to return the boy to his family safely. Ryder Williams is the 16-year-old lifeguard who rushed into the water to save a 10-year-old child who was overwhelmed by wave after wave. The incident was captured on camera, and the video has since been watched millions of times. That day, Williams says he was at “the waterline 15 yards downcoast of Tower 2 making a safety contact when I looked up and saw a child about 20 (yards) up from the tower lose his footing in ankle deep water. I radioed it in, threw my radio and sunglasses at the base of my tower as I ran toward the kid.” “I put my fins on my wrist, popped my buoy and entered the water to get ahold of the child. Due to the volatility of the water, I was unable to tube up the victim,” he wrote. “After the first wave I was unable to pull him out because he was limp and the waves were pushing so hard.” Santa Cruz Jul 28 Santa Cruz Jul 28 That’s when Williams explains he received help from another lifeguard, Aaron Bohnen. He added some beachgoers jumped in to help, but he “yelled at them all to get back to shore.” “Once Bohnen and I got the kid to shore I was instructed to get the med bag from Bohnen’s unit and we assessed the child,” Williams wrote. “Shortly after, I got back into my tower where I returned to provide lifeguard services for the rest of my shift.” Williams continues to say he is “grateful to have had the opportunity to return the child to his family safely.” “This is my job and I love what I do,” he wrote. “I’m thankful to my fellow lifeguards who perform rescues just like this every day.”

headlines.title: Group attack against laundromat worker in San Jose caught on camera
headlines.description: A San Jose man was brutally attacked early Wednesday morning at the laundromat where he’s worked for the past two years. The beating was caught on surveillance video. It’s spreading quickly online, not just because of how violent it is, but because it’s raising new concerns about the dangers many overnight workers face. Surveillance video shows a group confronting the 57-year-old worker. Without warning, one man throws a punch. The worker grabs a broom, trying to keep the group back. Instead, he’s shoved into a door and knocked onto the ground. Then the attack escalates. Several people swarm the victim, kicking and punching him before taking off. Police say it happened around 2 a.m. Wednesday. The worker suffered major head injuries but is expected to recover. Officers have arrested four people in connection with the attack. Investigators say the group also stole some of the victim’s belongings before leaving. The victim’s daughter identified him as 57-year-old Le. She says he’s now back home, recovering with stitches in his head. Nathalie Vera has more in the video report above.

headlines.title: Oakland Roots pay fees to play at Coliseum Saturday, but still owe rent
headlines.description: The Oakland Roots have cleared a major hurdle and will take the field at the Coliseum this Saturday. But the club still owes more than $1.4 million dollars in unpaid rent, and whether they’ll play the rest of their home schedule remains an open question. “I would say if you ever thought about going to a Roots game, now is the time to do it,” Alameda County Supervisor David Haubert said. Haubert, who sits on the Coliseum Authority Board, says the team has paid the fees needed to play this weekend. Going forward, the deal is simple. The roots must pay for each home game in advance or they don’t play. “We recognize if they don’t play, they can’t pay. So, it makes sense to let them play,” he said. The arrangement protects the Coliseum from taking on even more losses, while giving the roots a chance to generate the revenue they need. Pete Suratos has more in the video report above.

headlines.title: Shelter-in-place order issued in Alum Rock area of San Jose
headlines.description: A shelter-in-place order was issued Wednesday afternoon in the Alum Rock area of San Jose due to a possible barricaded person, officials said. The Santa Clara County Sheriff’s Office said deputies responded just after 3 p.m. to a reported domestic disturbance at a home on McKee Road near Eastside Drive. Initial indications pointed to a possible barricaded person, but deputies were still assessing the situation, the sheriff’s office said. A shelter-in-place order was issued for nearby homes out of an abundance of caution, according to the sheriff’s office. This is a developing story. Details may change as more information becomes available. Stay tuned for updates.

headlines.title: Bicyclist injured following crash involving vehicle in San Jose
headlines.description: A bicyclist is in critical condition following a vehicle collision in San Jose, police said. The crash was reported at 3:49 p.m. Wednesday in the area of King and McKee roads near Plata Arroyo Park. Police said the bicyclist was taken to a hospital and the driver remained on scene. The following road closures were in place due to the collision: Northbound and southbound King Road Eastbound and westbound McKee Road Police are asking the public to avoid the area while they investigate the crash. No other information was immediately available. This story uses functionality that may not work in our app. Click here to open the story in your web browser.

headlines.title: San Francisco rent report: 1- and 2-bedroom median rents hit record highs
headlines.description: Bay Area rent prices are hitting all-time highs and continuing to climb. Zumper’s National Rent Report released Tuesday breaks down the most expensive cities in the United States based on rent prices. For one-bedroom apartments, San Francisco checked in at No. 2 with a median rent of $4,180 – an all-time high for the city, according to Zumper. New York City topped the charts at $4,560. San Jose came in fifth at $2,770. For two-bedroom apartments, San Francisco ranked first at $6,020 and San Jose ranked third at $3,590. This marks the first time that Zumper has seen San Francisco’s two-bedroom rent exceed $6,000 in its records. San Francisco’s rent prices have been climbing fast over time. One-bedroom rent grew 3% month-over-month and 22.9% year-over-year. For two bedrooms, rent grew 5.6% month-over-month and 25.9% year-over-year. “AI sector hiring is pulling high earners back into the city, and there’s just minimal new construction in the pipeline, and our own data shows that active listings in San Francisco are down about 30% year-over-year,” said Crystal Chen, co-author of the Zumper report. headlines.title: Protestors in San Jose's Japantown rally against possible ICE facility in Gilroy
headlines.description: More than 100 people in San Jose’s Japantown gathered to oppose a possible ICE detention facility in Gilroy on Wednesday. Reverend John Oda pointed to injustices his uncle’s family faced when they were forced to live in an internment camp during World War II. “He fought and died for this country while his own family, my mother’s entire family, was placed behind barbed wire,” he said. Now he says he’s speaking out so history does not repeat itself. “When you see your government begin to sort human beings into categories of who deserves rights and who doesn’t, who deserves due process and who doesn’t, you do not stay quiet,” he said. This was a message echoed by many during the protest. “The thing we feared is happening again now. In World War II there were 75 confinement sites. Today there are over 200, and there are reports of horrifying, subhuman conditions,” SJ Nikkei Resisters Co-Founder Susan Hayase said. After Santa Clara County and the state sued the Trump administration to halt the project, federal officials agreed to pause construction until Sept. 9. But South Bay Congresswoman Zoe Lofren says the fight is far from over. “If that detention center is open and there is none right now in Northern California, it’s going to mean masked, armed, dangerous agents can fan out across Northern California and bring their reign of terror to our communities,” Lofren said. Which is why these activists are mobilizing, vowing to show up, speak out and stand together to protect all immigrants. NBC Bay Area reached out to the Department of Homeland Security for comment but hasn’t heard back.

headlines.title: Kith eyes location in San Francisco's Union Square, report says
headlines.description: New retail may be coming to Union Square in San Francisco. The San Francisco Chronicle reported Tuesday that high-end streetwear brand Kith is looking to open a space where the former Macy’s men’s store was located. A permit application was filed this year, and a permit was issued this month for retail. NBC Bay Area reached out to Kith through its website but did not immediately hear back. “Really exciting prospect for the district,” said Marisa Rodriguez with Union Square Alliance. “We’re thrilled because there has been a lot of momentum and a lot of energy and interest in Union Square. Feeling like we’re having a little bit of a renaissance. I’m really excited about what Union Square has in store over the next few years.” NBC Bay Area’s Christie Smith has more in the video report above.

headlines.title: Health officials announce 2 human cases of West Nile Virus in the South Bay
headlines.description: The West Nile Virus has infected two adults living in the South Bay, the Santa Clara County Public Health Department announced Wednesday. Additionally, for the first time this year, the agency and Vector Control have detected mosquitoes carrying the virus in various parts of the county. The Santa Clara County Public Health, as well as Vector Control, announced the two human cases but, due to privacy concerns, did not reveal their identities, how it happened, or where in the county they live. “The affected individuals are both adults. And both are currently recovering at home after receiving treatment. The two cases are unrelated. Both cases traveled domestically during their incubation period so we can’t say for certain where they were infected,” Assistant Public Health Officer Dr. Krishna Surasi said. Vector Control has done a lot to target mosquitoes already. Crews have conducted over 6,000 inspections, setting 1,800 traps and collecting about 20,000 mosquitoes for testing. Now, with new human cases, as well as finding two new pools containing West Nile positive mosquitoes, an abatement program including possible pesticide spraying will begin soon and Vector Control is asking the public to help by using repellent and getting rid of standing water. “Mosquitos only need about a bottle cap of water to begin developing. So, looking around your yard and dumping and draining any water you find is a huge help,” Jeremy Shannon with Vector Control said. Vector Control says it will conduct its normal operations for abatement, but are keeping up with new technology, including ‘Tornyol’, which uses mini-drones that, through AI, utilizes microphones and ultrasonics sensors to detect insects, especially mosquitos. It then kills them with the drone propellers. “It does seem like a novel technology to address adult mosquito populations which can spread disease. That being said, targeting individual adult mosquitoes may not be an efficient way to lower their populations and reduce risk,” Shannon said. So, at this point, Vector Control plans a more traditional approach, though exactly which measures will be used and what areas will be targeted will be announced later. But officials say communities affected will be notified in various ways 48-hours before the abatement starts.

headlines.title: Santa Rosa puts sales tax hike on November ballot
headlines.description: Santa Rosa voters will decide in November whether to extend and increase the city’s existing local sales tax to help fund public safety, road repairs and other city services as officials work to address ongoing budget shortfalls. The Santa Rosa City Council voted Tuesday to place the measure on the November 2026 ballot. If approved, it would reauthorize the city’s existing half-cent Measure Q sales tax at an updated 1-cent rate until ended by voters. City officials said the money would help support general services such as 911 emergency medical and fire response, police response to violent crimes, street and pothole repairs, and keeping public spaces safe and clean. City leaders said Santa Rosa has cut about $25 million in ongoing expenses over the past three fiscal years, including eliminating 82 positions, and has implemented pension reforms to help reduce a long-running structural budget deficit. If voters approve the measure, it is expected to generate about $46 million a year for city services. Mayor Mark Stapp said the city has already reduced spending on fire, police, street maintenance and other services because of budget pressures. He warned that without more local funding, more cuts are expected, including the planned rotating closure of fire stations that could slow emergency response times. Over 2,400 residents participated in a bilingual community outreach effort, with public safety and road maintenance emerging as the community’s top priorities, city officials said. A recent survey also found that up to 62% of respondents said they would support the tax measure. If approved, the measure would include independent audits and public disclosure of spending, according to city officials.

headlines.title: Crews stop forward progress of Ragione Fire in San Jose
headlines.description: Firefighters responded to a vegetation fire Wednesday afternoon in San Jose that burned between 0.5 and 1 acre, according to the San Jose Police Department. The fire, now known as the Ragione Fire, was reported near La Ragione Avenue and Albanese Circle. Officials said the fire spread at a slow rate. Traffic was impacted in the area as crews responded, and officials urged the public to avoid the area. SJPD said forward progress on the fire was stopped at 2 p.m.
